RoadmapPage.metaDescription: Track IvorySQL development progress, release schedules, and upcoming features.
RoadmapPage.heading: Welcome to Developers
RoadmapPage.intro: IvorySQL is a noncommercial, all volunteer, free software project, and as such there is no formal list of feature requirements required for development. We enjoy allowing developers to explore the topics of their choosing, though we also ensure that all new features committed to IvorySQL are thoroughly vetted by our community of contributors and committers.
RoadmapPage.minorReleasesDescription: The IvorySQL project aims to follow a predefined schedule, releasing at least one minor version per quarter. If additional releases are needed due to critical bug fixes or security issues, more releases will be made between these dates, so this list should be considered a minimum. IvorySQL closely follows PostgreSQL's release schedule, ensuring that a new minor version with the latest kernel updates will be released every quarter.

VulnerabilityManagementPage.metaDescription: IvorySQL vulnerability reporting process, severity assessment, and disclosure policy.
VulnerabilityManagementPage.heading: Vulnerability Management
VulnerabilityManagementPage.subheading: How the IvorySQL community handles security vulnerabilities - from reporting to disclosure.

response.title: Vulnerability Response
response.paragraph1: The IvorySQL community places a high priority on the security of its community edition. The IvorySQL Security Special Interest Group (SIG Security) is responsible for receiving, investigating, and disclosing security vulnerabilities related to the IvorySQL community. We encourage vulnerability researchers and industry organizations to proactively report suspected security vulnerabilities in IvorySQL to the SIG Security team. We aim to respond promptly, analyze, and resolve reported security issues or vulnerabilities.
response.paragraph2: As IvorySQL is based on PostgreSQL, vulnerabilities discovered and fixed in PostgreSQL also apply to IvorySQL. Our development team continuously monitors PostgreSQL community security information and promptly integrates PostgreSQL vulnerability patches into IvorySQL.

supportedVersions.title: Supported Versions
supportedVersions.paragraph: The vulnerability response process primarily supports the latest release of the IvorySQL community edition and its branch versions.

process.title: Vulnerability Handling Process
process.paragraph: Each security vulnerability is assigned a designated person for tracking and handling. This coordinator, a member of the IvorySQL SIG Security team, is responsible for overseeing the vulnerability remediation and disclosure. The end-to-end vulnerability handling process is outlined in the diagram below.
process.summary: In this document, we focus on three key aspects of the process: vulnerability reporting, vulnerability assessment, and vulnerability disclosure.

reporting.title: Vulnerability Reporting
reporting.paragraph: You can report potential security vulnerabilities in IvorySQL products by emailing the IvorySQL SIG Security team.

requiredInfo.title: Required Information for Reporting
requiredInfo.paragraph: To facilitate rapid confirmation and verification of suspected vulnerabilities, please include the following information in your vulnerability report email:

basicInfo.title: Basic Information
basicInfo.desc: Affected module, conditions triggering the vulnerability, and impact if successfully exploited.

technicalDetails.title: Technical Details
technicalDetails.desc: System configuration, identification methods, exploit description, PoC, and steps to reproduce.

reporterDetails.title: Reporter's Details
reporterDetails.desc: Organization and contact information of the reporter.

disclosurePlan.title: Disclosure Plan
disclosurePlan.desc: Any planned disclosure timeline or intentions by the reporter.

responseTime.title: Email Response Time
responseTime.paragraph: We will respond to suspected security vulnerabilities reported via email within 5 days and provide feedback on the progress of vulnerability handling to the reporter.

severity.title: Vulnerability Severity Assessment
severity.paragraph: We assess vulnerability severity using the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) standard:

disclosure.title: Vulnerability Disclosure
disclosure.paragraph: To protect IvorySQL users, the community strictly limits vulnerability information during investigation and remediation. Information is shared only with personnel directly involved in handling the vulnerability. We do not publicly disclose, discuss, or confirm security issues until a fix is released. Once fixed, an announcement will be published via the securityannounce@ivorysql.org mailing list.

ContributionGuidelinesPage.metaDescription: How to contribute to IvorySQL - from code patches to documentation, testing, and community participation.
ContributionGuidelinesPage.heroDescription: IvorySQL grows through contributions from developers, testers, documentation writers, translators, community advocates, and users around the world. This page summarizes the main ways to participate in the community and the current incentive policy. For step-by-step contribution instructions, please refer to the Contribution Guide on the IvorySQL documentation site.
ContributionGuidelinesPage.waysToContributeIntro: The IvorySQL community believes that open source should be approachable and that no contribution is too small. You can participate in a way that matches your background and interests:

waysToContribute.title: Code Contributions
waysToContribute.desc: Kernel development, feature iteration, bug fixes, plugin development, ecosystem tool adaptation, regression tests, and code review.

waysToContribute.title: Non-code Contributions
waysToContribute.desc: Issue reports, documentation improvements, technical translation, community Q&A, online or offline talks, case studies, migration experience sharing, and community promotion.

ContributionGuidelinesPage.waysToContributeOutro: If you are not ready to submit code yet, you can still make a meaningful contribution by reproducing issues, clarifying requirements, improving docs, or helping other users in community discussions.
ContributionGuidelinesPage.incentivesIntro: To encourage long-term participation, the IvorySQL community continues to improve how contributors are recognized and supported:

incentives.title: Recognition
incentives.desc: Contributors may receive community digital certificates and be featured on the official contributor wall to record their open-source footprint.

incentives.title: Mentorship
incentives.desc: The "Lighthouse" mentoring model helps contributors grow with technical guidance, one-on-one support, and code review feedback from experienced community members.

incentives.title: Community Opportunities
incentives.desc: Significant contributors may receive speaking, sharing, or participation opportunities at community events such as HOW and other technical activities.

incentives.title: Annual Incentives
incentives.desc: The community may select outstanding contributors for merchandise, public recognition, ecosystem exposure, and other collaboration opportunities.

ContributionGuidelinesPage.incentivesOutro: Specific arrangements may evolve with community programs, but sustained and valuable contributions are always taken seriously and recognized.
ContributionGuidelinesPage.communityProcessIntro: The IvorySQL community employs a closed-loop open-source collaboration process, ensuring that every step—from issue submission to version release—receives closed feedback and continuous improvement. This process encourages positive interaction between users and developers, allowing community development to evolve around actual needs.
ContributionGuidelinesPage.communityProcessStepsIntro: The entire closed-loop collaboration process is as follows:

processSteps.title: Submit Issue
processSteps.desc: Users or developers submit bugs, feature suggestions, or usage feedback on the GitHub Issues page.

processSteps.title: Discussion
processSteps.desc: Maintainers and community members discuss the issue, confirm its nature and priority, and add it to the ToDo List.

processSteps.title: Development Branch (Fork & Dev)
processSteps.desc: Developers claim the Issue, fork the repository, develop and test locally, and prepare to submit code.

processSteps.title: Submit Pull Request (PR)
processSteps.desc: Push the development branch to the forked repository and initiate a merge request to the upstream repository.

processSteps.title: Code Review
processSteps.desc: Maintainers or core developers review the PR, provide modification suggestions, and ensure quality.

processSteps.title: Merge to Main Branch
processSteps.desc: After approval, the PR is merged into the main branch, and the corresponding Issue is closed.

processSteps.title: Release
processSteps.desc: The project regularly releases new versions (minor versions quarterly, major versions annually), including the latest fixes and features.

processSteps.title: User Testing
processSteps.desc: Users upgrade to the new version, provide feedback on new issues, and new Issues are generated, forming a complete feedback loop.

steps.advance: Show leadership across the community and be nominated by at least two PMC Members.

steps.name: PMC Member
steps.tagline: A governance member shaping the project — the end of the path.
steps.summary: The top of the path: as a PMC Member you help decide where the project goes next.
points: Vote on the roadmap, releases, and new members
Nominate the next generation of Committers and PMC Members
steps.advance: Beyond this level, you can be elected to the Technical Committee or invited to the Expert Advisory Committee — the governance roles that shape the community itself.

RolesPage.mentorTitle: Support along the way — a “Beacon” mentor
mentorPoints: From Contributor on, you can request a Beacon mentor
Mentors are Committers, PMC Members, or Technical Committee members. They help you find your first contribution, review your work, and back your promotion
RolesPage.ctaHeading: Ready to take your first step?
RolesPage.ctaDesc: Start with one contribution — an issue report, a translation, a code review, or a pull request. Every accepted contribution moves you up the path.
RolesPage.govIntro: Community decisions are made by two separate governance bodies.

govCards.title: Technical Committee
govCards.desc: The community’s technical decision body, elected from PMC Members.
points: Reviews major architecture changes and approves release plans
Members keep their PMC Member status

govCards.title: Expert Advisory Committee
govCards.desc: An external advisory group of invited database specialists.
points: Independent of the five levels — not a promotion step
Advises on database technology, open-source trends, and ecosystem

RolesPage.contribTypesNote: Not just code: documentation translation, answering questions, organizing events, and open-source advocacy all count as contributions.
RolesPage.introLine2: Join as a User and grow step by step along a clear five-level path.
